title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
This incident shows a failure in the security layer between a user and a financial application. Fraudsters deployed an AI-generated fake website as an overlay on top of a legitimate trading app, creating a false display of account balances and transaction history that the victim could see on his screen. The deception worked because the victim had no way to verify what was real: the underlying app was legitimate, the returns appeared genuine, and the interface looked authentic.

The vulnerability exploited was a human one made exploitable by AI. The scammers used generated imagery to impersonate a financial system at scale, personalizing the fake displays to match each victim's supposed transactions and balances. What might have caught this earlier was skepticism at the moment the fraud began, when an unsolicited message from a stranger offered investment opportunity, or verification of account details through a channel the victim controlled independently rather than through screens the scammer could manipulate.

It is not established whether the trading app itself was compromised or merely spoofed, whether the AI-generated website was visually indistinguishable from the real one, or how the scammers gained access to overlay their fake display on the victim's device.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest through a legitimate-looking mobile trading app, gradually building trust by allowing him to make small trades and withdraw modest returns. Unknown to Jerry, scammers had created an AI-generated fake website that showed false investment balances on his screen, manipulating what he saw while the real money disappeared.

The couple discovered the fraud when Jerry attempted to make a larger withdrawal and the transaction failed, prompting him to call police. Gwinnett County investigators confirmed the app itself was real, but fraudsters had layered a deceptive overlay on top of it. Though devastated and embarrassed, Jerry and Mindy are publicly warning others about the scammers' sophisticated tactics. Police indicate victims rarely recover stolen funds in these cases, and the couple's children have started a GoFundMe to help them with daily expenses while they work with authorities.
